summary: PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 is a careful extraction, and its review did real work. I re-read the whole published article (Ann. of Math. 191 (2020), 893–948; the hash matches) against all 149 items. The mathematics stands. Every numbered statement is an item with the right hypotheses. The minor-arc repair (E1–E3, conservative range i > −4(tδ − (k−1))), the §6 lattice argument, the §7 Euler-product and rational-homotopy computations, and the compact-open counterexample to Lemma 7.2 and Conjecture 7.1 (E28, item 149) all re-derive. The 45 distinct source issues are genuine. The work breaks at its edges, in 13 findings: 2 medium and 11 low. (1) The review routed the Euler product of ζ_{F_q[t]} to a topology Part II, but FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 already planned it (medium). (2) Lang–Weil is routed here to FF.2, and by two later extractions to WC.5 (medium). (3)–(5) Configuration spaces, the Artin–Schreier sheaf and universal hypersurface monodromy are each also planned by a later extraction under another owner (low). (6) The review added a 'p odd' hypothesis to the Katz–Sarnak monodromy theorem, whose source holds in every characteristic ≠ ℓ (low). (7) The Frobenius cycle-type fact of Lemma 7.4 has no item, although Tau Ceti has it (low). (8) The auxiliary-prime choices rest on Dirichlet's theorem, and Corollary 2.9 never chooses ℓ (low). (9) E46 duplicates E35, and E38 contradicts E43 (low). (10) sourceVersions is missing (low). (11) Two items are routed to the wrong ES stages (low). (12) Items 66 and 72 ignore Mathlib's completion at infinity (low). (13) The report's headline counts are the pre-review ones (low).

Findings 2 and 4 touch FF.2 and cite PAPER-DELIGNE-80's Artin–Schreier item, which agrees with this extraction. Finding 1 cites FF.3 packet nodes. Finding 11 concerns ES stages audited in FIX-RT-AUDIT-07. None of these findings asks for a change to this session's own files.

Source, preprint. The paper is arXiv:1711.10451. The listing, read 30 September 2026, has v1 (28 Nov 2017), v2 (19 Jun 2019) and v3 (19 Feb 2020, latest). I fetched https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.10451v3 (49 pp.); its SHA-256 is 4518f888…9072, equal to the recorded hash.

Source, version of record. Ann. of Math. 191 (2020), 893–948, doi:10.4007/annals.2020.191.3.4, from https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v191-n3-p04-s.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026; SHA-256 f20c87e3…3c53, equal to the review's. The Annals page (annals.math.princeton.edu/2020/191-3/p04) gives Received 28 Nov 2017, Revised 8 Jan 2020, Accepted 14 Feb 2020, Published online 15 Apr 2020, and links no erratum. Crossref for the DOI has no update-to, relation or updated-by. I read all 56 published pages through pdftotext, §§1–7 and the references, against all 149 items. I read the §6 lattice argument, the §4 Goursat argument and the §7 Möbius and Hilton computations line by line.

Every numbered statement of the published text has an item with the right locator: Theorem 1.1, Corollaries 1.2 and 1.4, Conjecture 1.3, Remark 1.5, Lemma 2.1, Definition 2.3, Lemma 2.4(1)–(5), Propositions 2.5 and 2.6, Theorem 2.7, Lemma 2.8, Corollary 2.9, Lemmas 3.1–3.9, Corollary 3.10, Lemma 3.11, Corollary 3.12, Proposition 4.1, Lemmas 4.2–4.4, Definitions 5.1–5.2, Lemmas 5.3–5.4, Propositions 5.5, 5.7 and 5.8, Lemma 5.6, Lemma 6.1, Proposition 6.2, Lemma 6.4, Conjecture 7.1, Lemma 7.2, Definition 7.3 with (7.2), Lemma 7.4, Corollary 7.5, Lemma 7.6 and Theorem 7.7. Remark 2.2 and Remark 6.3 are motivational and are rightly not items. The inputs the paper uses are items: the SGA 4 list on p. 899, Stacks 012K, SGA 4 XIV 3.2, EGA IV 10.4.11 spreading out, [8, Lemma 8.5(i)] (schreier's 'linear_nontrivial_acyclic' API), [16, Lemma 13], [15, 8.2.5(2)], Hartshorne Ex. II.3.22(e), Lang–Weil, Lee Lemma 3.3.5, BV15 Lemma 2.8, CEF Th. 3.7, Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9, Broughton, Hilton, Sullivan and the dimension theorem. The only omissions I found are findings 7 and 8.

Main-theorem hypotheses and constants re-derived. Theorem 1.1: char K = 0, or char K > k with ℓ of even order; d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2; n > 2^k(k−1); range i > −4(⌊d/(k−1)⌋(n/2^k − k + 1) − 1). (1.1) is tδ ≥ 1, and n ≥ 2^k k suffices. Corollary 1.4: char K > k or 0, d ≥ k−1 ≥ 2, (1.1). Lemma 2.8's band m+1 ≤ i ≤ 2m for H_c^i(PConf_m), and Corollary 1.2's bands [1 − m(n−2), −m(n−3)], follow from it. Figure 1's support for n = 4 agrees with (1.3).

Minor-arc arithmetic. B(m) = n(2d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋/2^{k−2}) + 4(m+1) = 2dn − 4qδ + 4(r+1) for m = (k−1)q + r. E1 is right: kd = 9, b_5 = 1 is outside A_4. E2 is right: (k,d,n) = (3,4,24) gives B(5) = 192 > 188. The printed argument proves the sharp range only for (k,d) = (3,2): B(d) is sharp iff (k−1) | d, and the stratum m = d+1 exceeds it whenever m_0 > d. E3, minorsafe, comparisonsafe (i > −4(tδ − (k−1))), cohsupport, topdegeneration (m+s > 1 − 2(n−2)(n−3)) and irreduciblesafe (tδ > k−1) are right. So are E29's examples: (3,2,24) gives 923 groups and none in range; (3,10,24) gives 16.

§3 and §4 proofs re-read. Lemma 3.3 is legitimate: the T^{−1}-coefficient is linear in λ, because the λ^2 terms of F have lower degree. So are Lemma 3.6's two translations (m ≥ 2), Lemma 3.7's degree count (≤ 2n in both strata), the primitive-extension sequences of Lemma 4.2 for both parities of n, the rank N_1 = (1 − 1/k)((k−1)^{n_1} + 1) ≥ 6, the algebraic Goursat step (so_a ≇ sp_b for a ≥ 6) and the eigenvalue argument of Proposition 4.1. Items 30–39 and 138–142 match. Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9 read on its page (finding 6).

§5–§6 re-derived. Lemma 5.3 (ℓ^r ≡ −1 mod p) and Lemma 5.4 (Künneth). Proposition 5.5: the supremum over r ≤ N gives (dd + N(2^{k−1} − (k−1)))/2^{k−3}. Lemma 6.1's coefficient matching (T^{−i−1}, index i_1+…+i_{k−1}+i+1 ≤ kd). Lemma 6.4: R̂_{n+1} ≥ q^{⌈(c−a)/2⌉}, and the per-factor bounds q^s and q^{max(⌊(a−c)/2⌋,0)}. Iterated shrinking with a = d, c = d + (j−1)s. Proposition 6.2: |rα − a| < q^{−kd+m} with |r| ≤ q^m forces b ∈ A_m by Lemma 2.4(4); s = d − ⌊m/(k−1)⌋; the exponent (k−1)ns + (k−2)n(d−s) = dn(k−1) − n⌊m/(k−1)⌋; V ∩ Δ = cone over Sing Z = {0}. Items 42–53 and 66–81 match print, apart from findings 11 and 12, which concern owners and statuses.

§7 re-derived. (7.2) by the logarithm and Möbius inversion. Lemma 7.4's sign (−1)^{mn+i}, from χ = ((−1)^{n−1}N)^{c(σ)}(−1)^{(n−1)m} and ⟨χ, H_c^{m+i}⟩. The Euler product through ζ_{F_q[t]}(ks)^{e_k}. Corollary 7.5's weighted diagonal (only m ≤ d contribute when j ≤ d(n−3), because H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m) needs 1 ≤ i ≤ m). Lemma 7.6: Hilton multiplicities, the n-odd correction 1_{k≡2 mod 4}M(N, k/2) = −(2/k)Σ_{k/d odd}N^{k/d}μ(d), and the generating functions (1 + q^{−d})^{−e_k} and (1 − q^{−d})^{−e_k}. Theorem 7.7 needs j < 4(tδ−1) ≤ d(n−3). E4 (n = 3: π_0(Ω²X) = Z^N) is right. E5–E8 are right.

The extraction's own topology analysis, items 120–136, and the review's item 149. The escaping loop F_s = (T^dσ, ζT^dσ, 1, 0, …) with r(T) = 1/(4(1+|T|)) equals g outside a compact set for each s, is jointly continuous, and has end winding −1. By the tube lemma a filling disc would give a disc in C* with boundary of degree −1. For Fermat X with n ≥ 5, π_2 = π_3 = 0. At (k,d,n) = (3,2,40): t = 1, δ = 3, D = 74, and the Conjecture 7.1 range is 0 ≤ j < 8. The conservative range i > −4 contains i = −1, and cohsupport gives H_c^{2D−1} = 0 while H^1(Hco; Q) ≠ 0. E28 and item 149 stand.

All 46 source issues checked at their locators in the published text. E1–E45 are genuine, apart from E46 (a duplicate) and the E38/E43 inconsistency (finding 9). I found no further mistake in the paper beyond finding 8(b). Every issue is 'known: new'; no correction exists in print (Annals page, Crossref, arXiv v3).

findings.claim: Item 147 bundles three identities and routes all of them, as missing, to the topology Part II ConfigurationSpacesAndRationalLoops. Its part (1), the Euler product of the zeta function of F_q[t] over monic irreducibles, Σ_{f monic} U^{deg f} = (1−qU)^{−1} = ∏_g (1−U^{deg g})^{−1}, is function-field arithmetic that the atlas already plans. FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.5 plans Euler products by closed-point degree and the curve zeta function; F_q[t] is the case of P^1 with the degree-one point at infinity removed. The review's note that 'neither Mathlib ... nor any atlas stage has them' is wrong for the atlas half; FA.5 was in the atlas extract at the review's commit. Since then the FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums packet has planned the count of monic irreducibles and Gauss's product formula. Planning ζ_{F_q[t]} again in an algebraic-topology Part II duplicates both owners and puts arithmetic in a topology roadmap.
findings.evidence: Paper, published p. 943 (proof of Lemma 7.4): 'Σ_{f monic, squarefree} ((−1)^{n−1}N)^{ω(f)} q^{−deg(f)s} = ∏_{g prime}(1 + (−1)^{n−1}N q^{−deg(g)s}) = ∏_g ∏_k (1 − q^{−k deg(g)s})^{−e_k(N)} ... the right-hand side is equal to ∏_k ζ_{F_q[t]}(ks)^{e_k(N)} = ∏_k (1 − q^{1−ks})^{−e_k(N)}.' research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/FunctionFieldArithmetic.json, stage FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.5 'Zeta functions, Artin factors and Chebotarev': 'Construct Euler products by closed-point degree, identify the curve zeta function and its numerator ...'. The same sentence is in that file at commit 2126ef99 (the review's commit); the file dates from 2026-09-16. research/blueprint/packets/FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums.json (2026-09-25) has nodes FF.3/count-of-irreducible-polynomials ('Gauss's formula Σ_{d|n} d Π_F(n) = q^n, the Möbius formula ...') and FF.3/gauss-product-formula ('X^(q^n) − X = ∏_{d|n} ∏_{f ∈ monicIrreducibles F d} f'). Item 147's note: 'Neither Mathlib (no count of monic irreducibles at 082e2d3) nor any atlas stage has them.' Mathlib at 082e2d3 indeed has no such count; the atlas half of the sentence is false.
findings.fix: Split item 147. Part (1), the Euler product for all monic polynomials and ζ_{F_q[t]}(s) = (1 − q^{1−s})^{−1}, becomes status planned, citing FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.5 and, for the count of irreducibles, the packet nodes FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.3/count-of-irreducible-polynomials and FF.3/gauss-product-formula. Parts (2) and (3), the weighted squarefree product ∏_g(1 + aU^{deg g}) and its rewriting through the exponents e_k, are elementary formal identities used only by Lemma 7.4. They may stay missing with configEuler, but they import part (1) from FA.5 rather than proving it. Correct the note, and remove part (1) from route 7's item list and brief.

findings.claim: The review added the hypothesis 'p odd' to the item and called it the Katz–Sarnak theorem, saying that the characteristic hypotheses of Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9 'in particular p = 2 for even-dimensional hypersurfaces, must be read before the item is stated for all p ≠ ℓ'. I read them: the theorem has no such hypothesis. It holds on every geometric fibre of H_{n,d}[1/ℓ] over Z[1/ℓ], characteristic 2 included. The proof restricts to a sufficiently general Lefschetz pencil, which Deligne's Weil II 4.4.1 treats in characteristic 2. The item now states less than its source, and it contradicts route 6's brief ('in every characteristic distinct from ℓ'), which is right. The paper itself needs only p > k.
findings.evidence: Katz–Sarnak, Random Matrices, Frobenius Eigenvalues, and Monodromy (1999), p. 334 (author PDF page 343, SHA-256 39beb011e5fab2737bb131611f054221108128fbebbb7f62ba2de9a56f755dd5, the hash the extraction records; page image read): 'Theorem 11.4.9 ([De-Weil II, 4.4.1]). Suppose that d ≥ 3, that n ≥ 1, and that (n, d) ≠ (2, 3). For any prime l, the lisse sheaf Prim^n_l on H_{n,d}[1/l] has, on every geometric fibre of H_{n,d}[1/l]/Z[1/l], the group G_geom given by Sp(prim(n, d)), if n odd, O(prim(n, d)), if n even.' Proof: 'Let us examine the situation in a given characteristic p ≠ l ... it suffices to show that a sufficiently general Lefschetz pencil has the asserted G_geom.' The even case needs 'n(d − 2) ≥ 4', which for even n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3 excludes only (2, 3). Item 34 now reads: 'let p = char of the base field satisfy p ≠ ℓ and p odd (p > k suffices for the paper)'.
findings.fix: Restore the source statement in item 34: for k ≥ 3, r ≥ 2 and (r−1, k) ≠ (2, 3), over every algebraically closed field of characteristic p ≠ ℓ (including p = 2), G_geom(Prim_{r,k}) is Sp for r−1 odd and O for r−1 even. Say that in characteristic 2 the proof uses a sufficiently general pencil as in Weil II 4.4.1, and that the paper needs only p > k. Replace the review note with a record of this reading.

findings.where: PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/configtrace (item 87) and PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/configEuler (item 89); proof of Lemma 7.4
findings.claim: Lemma 7.4 evaluates an S_m-character at the Frobenius of a squarefree polynomial f. It uses that the Frobenius conjugacy class in S_m has one cycle per irreducible factor of f, of length the factor's degree, so that the number of cycles is ω(f). No item states this, and neither configtrace nor configEuler depends on it. Tau Ceti has it at the pinned commit, as the statement that the Frobenius orbits on the roots of g match the monic irreducible factors, each orbit having the factor's degree as its size.
findings.evidence: Paper, published p. 942: 'This is a conjugacy class in S_m with one cycle for each irreducible factor of the polynomial, of length equal to the degree of the irreducible factor.' Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/FrobeniusOrbits.lean:62 TauCeti.FiniteField.natCard_orbit_eq_natDegree_factor ('The size of a Frobenius orbit on the roots of g is the degree of the matching monic irreducible factor of g, along the bijection TauCeti.orbitQuotientEquivFactors'). Also :71 TauCeti.FiniteField.exists_orbit_eq_rootSet_factor, :54 image_val_orbit_gal_eq_orbit, and TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Orbits.lean:323 orbitQuotientEquivFactors. All were read at f790474.
findings.fix: Add a library item: for squarefree monic f of degree m over F_q, the q-power Frobenius permutes the roots of f with one orbit per monic irreducible factor, of size its degree. Its cycle type is therefore the multiset of factor degrees, and its number of cycles is ω(f). Credit tauceti:TauCeti.FiniteField.natCard_orbit_eq_natDegree_factor, tauceti:TauCeti.FiniteField.exists_orbit_eq_rootSet_factor and tauceti:TauCeti.orbitQuotientEquivFactors. Add it to dependsOn of configtrace and configEuler.

findings.claim: Two choices of auxiliary primes are used but not itemised. (a) Theorem 1.1 in characteristic 0 needs a prime p > k, among the residue characteristics of an open subset of Spec R, such that ℓ has even order mod p. The paper takes ℓ to be a quadratic non-residue mod p via quadratic reciprocity. This needs infinitely many primes in a residue class modulo 4ℓ, which is Dirichlet's theorem. (b) Corollaries 1.4 and 2.9 in characteristic p > k contain no ℓ, but their proof invokes Corollary 1.2 and Theorem 1.1. Those require ℓ ≠ p of even order mod p, and the paper never says that such ℓ exists. It does, for example any prime ℓ ≡ −1 mod p, again by Dirichlet. The spread item mentions (a) in passing; nothing covers (b). Mathlib has both inputs.
findings.evidence: Paper, published pp. 906–907: 'we can choose one of characteristic p with p > k and where ℓ has even order mod p (e.g., by using quadratic reciprocity to choose p so that ℓ is a quadratic non-residue mod p).' Corollary 2.9, p. 907: 'Let K be a field with char(K) > k if char(K) ≠ 0. Assume that d ⩾ k−1 ⩾ 2 and that (1.1) holds.' Proof, p. 908: 'When i > 0 this follows from Corollary 1.2 ...'. Corollary 1.2, p. 895: 'If char(K) ≠ 0, then assume that char(K) > k and ℓ has even order modulo char(K).' Mathlib 082e2d3: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:442 Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod ('if a : ZMod q is a unit, then ... ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a'); Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/QuadraticReciprocity.lean:107 legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity and :74 ZMod.exists_sq_eq_two_iff.
findings.fix: Add a library item: for a prime ℓ and any bound B there is a prime p > B with ℓ of even order mod p. Examples are p with ℓ a quadratic non-residue, or ℓ ≡ −1 mod p for a fixed p, both by Dirichlet. Credit mathlib:Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod and mathlib:legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity. Make spread and irreduciblesafe depend on it; irreduciblesafe needs the choice of ℓ for a given p. Add a source issue (kind gap, affects nothing, known new) at Corollary 2.9 and its proof, pp. 907–908: the corollary has no ℓ, while Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 need ℓ of even order mod char K. The correction is to choose a prime ℓ ≡ −1 mod char K, which exists by Dirichlet.

findings.where: PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20 sourceIssues E46 and E35, E38 and E43
findings.claim: E46, added by the review, is the same finding as E35: the same sentence on p. 897, 'In Section 6 ...', corrected to 'Section 7'. E46's own locator says 'the coordinator may deduplicate'. Both reach research/errata/REGISTER.md as separate entries, so the paper's count of confirmed mistakes is inflated by one. E38 (a misprint) and E43 (a gap) also overlap on Remark 1.5, and they disagree. E38's reason asserts that the dimension count is right because the scheme is 'non-empty over K̄ via constant solutions'. E43 and item 64 show that the scheme is empty for n = 2.
findings.evidence: result.json sourceIssues: E35 printed 'In Section 6 we shall investigate a potential space with this property ...', correction 'Section 7 (Topological interpretation, p.939)'; E46 has the same printed text and correction 'In Section 7', locator '§1, before Conjecture 1.3, p. 897 ... the coordinator may deduplicate.' research/errata/REGISTER.md has both, at lines 2014 (E35) and 2026 (E46). Published pp. 898–899 (Remark 1.5) have no hypothesis n ≥ 3.
findings.fix: Delete E46, or mark it as a duplicate of E35 so that scripts/errata.py drops it, and regenerate REGISTER.md. In E38's reason replace 'non-empty over K̄ via constant solutions' with 'non-empty over K̄ via constant solutions when n ≥ 3; see E43 for n = 2'.

findings.where: route 1 (source ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0–ES.1): PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/polynomialbox (item 81) and PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/polardimension (item 80)
findings.claim: Route 1 sends two items to ES.0–ES.1 whose content is not in those stages. ES.0 covers Weyl differencing, van der Corput, stationary phase and completion of sums; ES.1 covers orthogonality identities and major and minor arcs. polynomialbox is Browning–Vishe's uniform bound for F_q[T]-points of bounded height on an affine variety, a point-counting theorem with explicit uniformity. That is ES.5's subject ('counting rational/integral points, with heights and uniformity parameters explicit'). polardimension is an algebro-geometric dimension bound for the polar-zero variety of the leading form, proved by the affine dimension theorem. Its only supplier, the review's rev-affine-dimension-theorem-for-intersections, went to GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces. As routed, the ES.0–ES.1 blueprint would own a dimension theorem it has no supplier for.
findings.evidence: data/atlas.json: ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.0 'Develop Weyl differencing, van der Corput, stationary phase and completion of sums ...'; ES.1 'Prove exact orthogonality identities translating integral solutions into torus integrals of exponential sums; define major/minor arcs ...'; ES.5 'Add determinant-method and arithmetic-geometric comparison routes for counting rational/integral points, with heights and uniformity parameters explicit'. Item 81: 'For affine V ⊂ A^N over F_q(T), defined over F_q[T], of dimension e and degree Δ, the number of polynomial points with |u| < q^h is O_{Δ,N}(q^{he}) ... uniformly in q.' Item 80: 'W = {Ψ_1 = ⋯ = Ψ_n = 0} ⊂ A^{n(k−1)} has dim W ≤ n(k−2): its intersection with the diagonal A^n is only 0, and the affine dimension inequality gives the bound.' Paper p. 939: '0 = dim(V ∩ Δ) ⩾ dim V + dim Δ − (k − 1)n'.
findings.fix: Route polynomialbox to ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.5, as a separate source-route entry. Move polardimension to the GeometricCircleMethodAndMappingSpaces Part II beside rev-affine-dimension-theorem-for-intersections, and add that item to its dependsOn. Keep the genuinely Weyl-differencing items (polarization, polarlocus, topphase, Nalpha, Nidentity, Nbound, itershrink, shortzero) at ES.0–ES.1.

findings.claim: Items 66 and 72 are missing, and route 5's brief tells the new Part II to build on Mathlib's LaurentSeries, reading its variable as T^{−1}. Mathlib at the pin already has the completion of F_q(T) at infinity with its valuation, which is exactly the field and absolute value of §6.
